Convert a gtsummary table into a flextable matching HVTI CORR's table rules

Source: R/hv-man-table.R
hv_man_table.Rd

Stage 2 of the %summarytable split: shapes the table. The macro controlled this with STYLE= and PAGE=. style = is the equivalent of STYLE=: tables are drawn in a style named by its role, "report" (the default, described below) or "manuscript". PAGE= has none; pages are US Letter, turning landscape when the table is wide.

Usage

hv_man_table(
  tbl,
  font = "Times New Roman",
  font_size = 12,
  digits = 2,
  style = "report",
  layout = "compare",
  ...
)

Arguments

tbl

A gtsummary table object (must support as_flex_table()). A table from hv_tbl_summary() is split as described above; any other gtsummary object renders as-is.

font

Font family. Default "Times New Roman" (house rule). Any single non-empty string is accepted: flextable silently substitutes an unknown font name, so a typo would otherwise pass unnoticed, while a deliberate override is legitimate.

font_size

Font size in points. Default 12; pass 11 for wide tables, per house rule 5. No other values are permitted.

digits

Kept for interface symmetry with future callers; currently unused (rounding is controlled upstream via tbl_summary(digits = ...)). Reserved so a future version can enforce sig-fig rounding centrally without a breaking signature change.

style

A style name, "report" (default) or "manuscript", or a style from hv_table_style(). "manuscript" needs an hv_tbl_summary() table, refuses font and font_size, and in the compare layout refuses continuous_stat = "both".

layout

The manuscript style's layout, chosen by what the table does: "compare" (default), one overall n column for groups it compares, or "describe", a count beside each group, for cohorts or repeated measures it describes side by side. Either shows an Overall column and comparison columns when the table carries them. Only with style = "manuscript".

...

Not used. Present so that %summarytable parameter names produce an error naming the argument to use instead.

Value

A flextable object, ready for hv_man_table_save(). In the report style it has a single header row and no merged cells; in the manuscript style a two-row header. Its hv_style attribute holds the style, which the saver and hv_man_table_display() read. Input from hv_tbl_summary() retains its hv_footnotes attribute so the saver's default dagger follows the table's continuous statistic.

Details

The "manuscript" style lays out a comparison table as the journal submissions did: a full grid, a two-row header with the grouping's name spanning its levels, one overall n column, shaded section rows that span the table, a bold header, and no font of its own, so the table takes the body font of the document it is saved into. It needs a table from hv_tbl_summary(), and hv_man_table_save() requires a caption for it. See hv_table_style() for the properties of each style, and the Table styles article, which draws one table in each style and layout beside the matrix of their properties and says which house rules each style keeps.

The rest of this page describes the "report" style.

You give this a gtsummary::tbl_summary() (or any gtsummary table object supporting gtsummary::as_flex_table()), and you get back a flextable that already complies with HVTI CORR's "Table Construction for Manuscripts" rules: a single, non-merged header row (no spanning parent cells over grouped columns), no merged row-group section-header cells, a left-justified label column, and Times New Roman at the house font size. Section rows are shaded across every cell, unmerged, in the style's fill (#CAEDFB by default), and the header is bold.

gtsummary::as_flex_table() already emits one header row per group with self-contained labels (e.g. "B\nN = 45"), not a merged spanning header. Any merged region is undone with flextable::merge_none(). That satisfies the "format the table as flat as possible ... simple non-merged column titles" rule.

The sections of an hv_tbl_summary() table (its groups names, such as "Demography") become bold header rows in the label column, each immediately above its first variable, rather than a column of their own.

Rounding, %-free percentage cells, and ±-without-spaces formatting are yours to control, via the statistic/digits arguments to gtsummary::tbl_summary(); see the package README for a worked example using gtsummary::style_sigfig() for 2-significant-figure rounding.

A manuscript table that describes cohorts or repeated measures side by side, rather than comparing groups, takes layout = "describe": each group spans its own count and statistic, so every group has its count. Everything else is the comparison layout's. The JTCVS functions, whose layout this is, are deprecated.

A table from hv_tbl_summary() works in every style and layout. That function writes each cell as "{N_nonmiss} ||| {stat}", and this one splits the two apart into a flat No. column immediately before the statistic it counts. Those are the same two values the describe layout puts under each group's spanning header, without the merge. House rule 8 wants that non-missing count, and hv_man_footnotes()'s * footnote describes it, so it is kept rather than discarded. A plain gtsummary::tbl_summary() table carries no such convention and passes through unchanged.

None of gtsummary's own footnotes reach the table: as_flex_table() writes them as a footer row and a raised digit inside the table, and house rule 13 puts notes below it. hv_tbl_summary() says what they said in the notes hv_man_table_save() writes: the tests behind the p-values in the dagger note, and CI in the key.

Common mistakes

Cells read 98 ||| 46 (32, 63). You are on a version before the split; upgrade. ||| is the internal separator hv_tbl_summary() writes between the count and the statistic, never intended to reach a rendered table.

"tbl was not built with the {N_nonmiss} ||| {stat} convention." Only some cells carry the separator, which means statistic was set for part of the table. Splitting would leave the rest blank, so it is rejected. Either apply the convention to every variable or to none; hv_tbl_summary() does the former for you.

"font_size must be 11 or 12." House rule 5. Use 11 only for wide tables.

"font and font_size set the report style." You passed one with style = "manuscript". That style sets no font, so the table takes the font of the document it is saved into. Drop the argument, or use style = "report".

The compare layout refuses a continuous_stat = "both" table. That table has a column for the median and another for the mean and SD, which the compare layout's one statistic column per group cannot lay out. Build the table with "median" or "mean", or draw it with layout = "describe" or the report style, which show both.

The manuscript style refuses a table not built by hv_tbl_summary(). The layout reads the overall count and the grouping's name that function records. Build the table with it.

"layout chooses between the manuscript style's layouts." You named a layout with the report style, which has one. Drop layout, or add style = "manuscript".

See also

hv_man_table_save() to write the result to a compliant .docx with footnotes and an abbreviation key. hv_table_style() for each style's properties.

Examples

library(gtsummary)
tbl <- tbl_summary(trial, by = trt, include = c(age, grade))
ft <- hv_man_table(tbl)
ft2 <- hv_man_table(
  hv_tbl_summary(
    trial, by = "trt", groups = list(A = c("age", "grade")),
    continuous = "age", categorical = "grade"
  ),
  style = "manuscript", layout = "describe"
)
